newsitem.title: USA: MCA ex-counsel testifies in Viacom dispute.
newsitem.headline: MCA ex-counsel testifies in Viacom dispute.

text.p: A former MCA Inc general counsel testified Tuesday in the Delaware Chancery Court that the company intended a provision in an agreement setting up a joint cable television venture to apply to "successors" of the original partners.
The testimony opened a scheduled four-week trial involving Viacom, MCA's current partner in the USA Networks cable venture. MCA is a unit of Seagram Co Ltd.
At issue is a provision that prohibits ownership of basic cable-television networks or pay-per-view programming services outside the partnership.
Viacom inherited the USA Networks partnership through its acquisition in 1993 of Paramount Communications Inc, one of the original partners in the venture.

On Tuesday, former MCA general counsel Robert Hadl, who ended nearly 20 years with MCA after its buyout by Seagram last year, said the non-compete or exclusivity provision was included in the original 1981 agreement.
Hadl said the intent of the provision had been to include all "successors and assigns" of the original partners despite Viacom's assertion to the contrary.
"We wanted to be sure that everyone in the corporate hierarchy was going to be bound...upwards, downwards and sidewards," Hadl said under questioning by MCA attorney Herbert Wachtell.
In cross-examination, Viacom attorney Anthony Clark repeatedly tried to get Hadl to admit that MCA had not applied the non-compete or exclusivity provision against another former partner, Time Inc.

In court documents, Viacom alleges Seagram chief executive Edgar Bronfman Jr in April told Viacom chairman Sumner Redstone that "if Viacom were not willing to sell its partnership interest to MCA, MCA would sue."
